script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for July 14. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Blame is tempting.  It shifts weight off your shoulders.  But every time you blame circumstances, other people, or bad luck, you give away power.

If you're responsible, you have power to change things. If circumstances are responsible, you're helpless. Even when something isn't your fault, asking 'what can I do about it?' is more useful than assigning blame. Extreme performers often take extreme responsibility.  Athletes blame themselves for team losses.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Power and responsibility are inseparable.  You can't have control without accepting ownership.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Ownership Shift - Blame to Power.

Here's your activity: Identify something you've blamed on external factors—circumstances, other people, bad luck. Ask: What part of this am I responsible for? What could I do differently? Shifting from blame to ownership doesn't add guilt; it adds power. This helps you convert blame into ownership.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about owning what you do can be applied to ownership shift - blame to power. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
